articleTitle: 4-Phase Series-capacitor Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The series-capacitor (SC) converter is an attractive choice due to its capacity for achieving a high step-down conversion ratio, reducing voltage stress on switching devices, and maintaining inherent current balance. To enhance power capacity and minimize output current fluctuations, a multi-phase series-capacitor configuration was introduced. However, as the number of phases increases, the operational range of the converter proportionally decreases by a factor of n, where n represents the number of phases. Consequently, the suitability of the multi-phase SC topology diminishes. This study introduces a 4-phase series-capacitor (4P-SC) converter that extends the conventional SC structure to attain higher output power. Moreover, the proposed converter reduces output current ripple and requires only half the number of current sensors compared to the conventional 4-phase buck converter (4P-IBC). In this paper, the proposed structure is validated by simulation.

articleTitle: Average Block Error Rate Analysis of IRS-Aided NOMA Short-Packet Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the average block error rate (BLER) of an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) assisted non-orthogonal multiple-access (NOMA) in short-packet communications (SPC) over Nakagami-m fading channels. In the considered system, a base station wishes to communicate with two users by using NOMA and SPC techniques with the aid of an IRS. We derive not only the closed-form expressions for the average approximate BLER of users but also the average asymptotic BLER in a high transmit signal-to-noise ratio. Monte Carlo simulations are conducted to verify the derived analytical BLER expressions. The simulation results also unveil the impact of the number of IRS elements and blocklength on system BLER performance.

articleTitle: Simplified Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation for Four-Level Neutral Point Clamped Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Multilevel inverters have become a suitable candidate for high power applications due to their output performance and power density. In particular, Four-level neutral-point-clamped inverter (NPC) has received a lot of attention due to the demands of commercial and industrial applications requiring higher DC link voltages and ever-improved power quality compared to three-level inverter. One of the primary challenges for multilevel inverters is that the space vector diagram for modulation schemes becomes complex as the number of voltage levels increases. This paper presents a Simplified space vector pulse width modulation (SSVPWM) for four-level neutral point clamped inverter to overcome this issue. This method reduces the quantity of sub-regions for a four-level inverter space vector diagram, compared to the conventional space vector PWM method. Furthermore, the space vector diagram of the four-level converter is transformed into a two-level space vector diagram, which reduces complexity and computation burden. Performance of the SSVPWM method is verified through the simulation results.

articleTitle: Load Profile-Based Fine-Tuning of Piecewise Droop Control for Enhanced DC Microgrid Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Droop control has emerged as a popular autonomous control technique for DC microgrids, but it is impacted by cable impedance mismatches. The presence of these system mismatches causes a degradation in the current sharing performance and system stability. In this paper, a tunning approach based on the load profile is presented to define piecewise droop control for enhancing the performance of DC microgrids. The proposed method involves analyzing the load current distribution and the characteristics of droop control to determine an enhanced piecewise current setpoint. Also, a comparison is made between the proposed approach and both linear and nonlinear droop-based methods. Through analysis and simulations, the results demonstrate that the load profile-based fine-tuning method can substantially improve current sharing within a specific operating region.

articleTitle: Soft-start Active-clamp Isolated Full-bridge Current-fed DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The conventional isolated full-bridge current-fed (FB-CF) DC-DC converter suffers two critical problems, voltage spike across switches and inrush current at start-up. This paper proposed a method for an active-clamp FB-CF converter. The proposed converter can solve both critical issues with the suggested method without any auxiliary circuit or extra components. The operation of the converter is investigated under both steady-state and start-up periods. The method is verified by simulation and experiments with a 1 kW prototype.

articleTitle: Design and Deployment of MRHeart Software to Process Cardiac MRI Images on Workstation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) is considered one of the most modern cardiovascular diagnostic and monitoring methods. Currently, this technique is widely applied in coronary artery disease, congenital heart disease, cardiomyopathy, heart valve, etc. Quantitative assessment of the diseased myocardium on CMRI plays an important role in the diagnosis and prognosis of cardiovascular disease. The aim of this work is to design and deploy a software to extract the Region Of Interest (ROI) from the cardiac MRI images and calculate the size, mass, volume, and blood flow of the heart using Simpson’s rule. DICOM (Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine) medical images are obtained directly and automatically from the MRI modality through the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) at Telemedicine and Mobile Healthcare lab, Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology. The experimental investigation of the proposed work shows that the cardiovascular diagnostic using our software offers faster assessment of cardiac parameters than only with traditional doctors.

articleTitle: Speed Sensorless Vector Control of Induction Motor Using MRAC Estimator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In recent years, many speed estimators have been developed in order to eliminate the use of the shaft speed sensor. Among them, Model Reference Adjustable Control (MRAC) is the simplest close-loop speed estimator that based on a machine model. In this paper, speed sensorless vector control for induction motor using MRAC is presented and simulated by Matlab/Simulink. Performance of the sensorless drive has verified the accuracy and effectiveness of the MRAC estimator.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Switching Controller for an Industrial Crane System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Sliding mode control is a powerful method for addressing uncertainties in nonlinear dynamic systems. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis, redesign, and comparison of different sliding mode controllers for an industrial crane system that transports underwater objects. To improve the stability of the system and reduce or eliminate chattering, a family of continuous switching functions was applied during the redesign of the switching control part. A comparative study of these proposed functions was conducted to evaluate their performance criteria in two separate stages: the optimal gain-finding stage and the ideal shaping coefficient-identifying stage. In order to validate the efficiency and robustness of the newly designed controllers, numerical results obtained using both the novel and the traditional approaches were processed using statistical metrics and compared. As expected, the new sliding mode controllers delivered excellent simulation results for the crane system and exhibited minimal visible chattering as well as tracking errors. Moreover, a set of optimal feedback gains for the switching control part was determined, and an ideal shaping coefficient for each continuous switching function was found.

articleTitle: Seamless Grid Transfer Scheme for Distributed Generation Units Utilizing The Generalized Voltage Droop Control Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This study conducts an analytical investigation of an inverter using generalized droop control (GDC) and improves GDC synchronization part. The proposed approach simplifies the synchronization part of GDC to deliver a satisfactory control performance. This feature enables the inverter utilizing GDC to exhibit noticeably smoother output voltage and frequency changes during grid outages. The analysis and comparison between the improved GDC and droop control are described. Also, a simplified GDC transfer function is derived. The study assertions are proven by simulation results.

articleTitle: Development of Path Tracking and Obstacle Avoidance based on an Advanced Potential Field Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper proposes a new method that combines path tracking and obstacle avoidance for a differential drive mobile robot based on the Advanced Potential Field Controller (APFC) to increase stability and safety for robot operation. In conventional methods, the transition between path following and obstacle avoidance is typically achieved through a simple switch, which does not ensure the robot returns to the original path after avoiding the obstacle. The proposed methods integrate the Repulsive Potential Field (RPF) and Attractive Potential Field (APF), effectively solving this issue and enhancing smooth navigation in static environments. The RPF is utilized to steer the robot away from obstacles, while the APF is employed to redirect the robot back to its path after obstacle avoidance. The algorithm is verified on the designed robot, and experimental results provide efficiency in achieving autonomous robot navigation.

articleTitle: Massive MIMO Power Allocation Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper studies the power allocation strategy in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless networks to maximize the sum spectral efficiency (SE) in the downlink transmission. Different from the traditional methods capitalizing on nonlinear optimization algorithms which require high computational complexity, we invoke a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework to obtain the optimal power allocation. Specifically, from the power allocation design problem for massive MIMO networks, we develop an algorithm leveraging a twin-delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) framework to seek the optimal policy that maximizes the expected cumulative long-term reward in terms of the SE. The numerical results are provided to demonstrate the achievable SE obtained from the DRL framework in comparison with those from optimization algorithms.

articleTitle: Efficient Power Allocation Scheme for Hybrid Energy Storage Systems in Autonomous DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the distribution of energy within a DC microgrid, specifically highlighting the utilization of different storage sources such as supercapacitors and photovoltaic (PV) generators. In the presence of abnormal load operation, abrupt changes in load power can result in inadequate and inefficient current sharing within the DC microgrid. Thus, an integrated droop control (IDC) method is proposed to automatically control energy sharing by expanding the conventional voltage droop controller into a capacitor-based droop controller to supplement necessary characteristics in the system operation at high frequencies. By combining two virtual capacitors and resistor droop controllers, it is possible to achieve improved load current response, thanks to the high-frequency oscillation compensation of the supercapacitor and the stable energy supply at low frequencies provided by the PV generator. To apply the IDC method to the system model, the system parameter design process is carried out, calculated, and analyzed for the response in different frequency ranges to achieve automatic and stable voltage control. Simulations have been conducted to confirm the effectiveness of this IDC strategy.

articleTitle: Kinematic Model and Stable Control Law Proposed for Four Mecanum Wheeled Mobile Robot Platform Based on Lyapunov Stability Criterion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Transportation in warehouses and production workshops is a matter of urgency today. Most warehouses arrange routes for circulation along the shelves, transportation vehicles will move on this road to perform the task of exporting or importing goods. Routes will be arranged to move in one direction because vehicles do not have enough space to turn around in cramped warehouses. This causes many difficulties in planning the trajectory for transportation vehicles, especially self-propelled vehicles. In order to have an appropriate transportation plan, it is necessary to solve many problems, including: reasonable transport equipment, sufficient number of devices, optimal route layout, algorithm of operation center for Positioning and Navigation of transportation equipment. This study proposes a method for transportation using an omnidirectional automated guided vehicle (AGV). The AGV's omnidirectional mobility is supported by the mecanum wheels, so vehicles can move in multiple directions on the road without turning, even at a junction or an intersection. This study consists of two parts, the first part focuses on kinematic modeling for mecanum wheels and extends to robot’s platform using four mecanum wheels. Part two proposes a diagram to calculate the errors of the robot compared to a reference tracking line, design a control law based on the Lyapunov stability criterion. The stability of the control law is verified and confirmed by simulation on Matlab environment.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis for Stirred-Tank Heating Process using KPCA and ANN Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Flexible manufacturing processes, which are considered as being crucial to the fourth industrial revolution, are playing more and more essential role in modern industry nowaday. Almost all hardware and software manufacturers made every effort to ensure optimal performance with the lowest defection as possible. However, beside the high-accuracy operation of actuators, chemical processing industry specifically call for more stringent conditions. Even a tiny difference in the outcome of chemical reactions can result in subpar quality. As a result, monitoring operations must be quick and accurate enough to identify and isolate errors whenever system issues arise. This research investigates a data-driven estimation-based technique for process fault detection and diagnostic. According to this method, the discrepancy between the process responses and the estimated model responses is used to identify all process defects. The Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) is used to identify issues for fault detection in conjunction with an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) fault classifier model. The suggested approach has been validated using the stirred-tank heating process. The simulation results demonstrate how successful the suggested approach is.

articleTitle: An 8-16 GHz 1-Channel Transceiver 65nm CMOS Beamformer IC
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: A phased-array 1-channel transceiver 65nm CMOS beamformer IC working over 8-16 GHz covering the X and Ku band which are used in radar and satellite applications is reported in this paper. Besides the low noise amplifier (LNA) and the power amplifier (PA), each path has a phase shifter (PS) and a variable gain amplifier (VGA) which provide phase and gain adjustment for beam steering angle control and beam tapering control in a typical beamforming system. The measurement results show that the phase-compensated VGA provides 15 dB of gain range in 0.25 dB step with rms gain error of 0.27 dB. The active vector modulator phase shifter has 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> of phase range control, 2.8125<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> of phase step, 3.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> of rms phase error. The TX path has the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> of 21.3 dB, the NF of 13.8 dB, the OIP3, the saturated power P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SAT</inf> , and OP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> of 18, 11 dBm and 9 dBm while the RX path has the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> of 11.4 dB, NF of 6.3 dB, IP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> of -7 dBm and IIP3 of 0.5 dBm. The chip consumes the DC power of 303 mW for the TX path and 103 mW for the RX path. The beamformer has a compact size of 2275x1909 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality Application in Digital Automation Laboratory
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Traditional automation engineering education using physical training equipment while quite effective, suffers from several limitations in the case there is no equipment access, which can be due to many reasons such as social distancing or financial difficulties. This article proposes a solution to overcome these limitations with the combinational use of mixed reality (MR), which helps the student get used to training equipment they have no access to, and augmented reality (AR), which brings intuitive visualization into real equipment practice.

articleTitle: Initial Rotor Position Estimation of PMSM Based on DC-Link Voltage Dip Analysis Using Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper proposes an initial rotor position estimation scheme of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM). It is based on an analysis of the DC-link voltage dips that result from voltage pulse injection, where a neural network (NN) is applied. The effect of magnetic saturation due to sequential voltage injections to different phases and magnetic flux is utilized to incur a variation in inductance. The injected voltage pulse causes a dip in the DC-link voltage. The change in inductance and consequently the voltage dip depend on the rotor position. The NN is used to analyze the dips in the measured DC-link voltage, where the additional process needed to determine the rotor polarity is eliminated since the measured voltage differs in accordance with the polarity. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been verified through the simulation, with an absolute average error of 0.157° in the estimated initial position. The proposed method is used to estimate the initial rotor position, 151°, which is then utilized to perform the starting ramp speed operation; 0 - 1200 rpm.

articleTitle: A simple approach to extract model for a floating-gate transistor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: A new and simple approach to studying the model extraction is described in this work. This paper proposed the use of a standard industrial ICCAP tool in investigating DC model extraction for a floating-gate transistor which is well-known as the core element of many designs. The Level 3 model is deployed in modeling the transistor relying on the essential input requirements. The relations of drain current versus control gate voltage and drain voltage are presented with different geometries of width and length. The results proved excellent accuracy at large dimensions and promising at the smaller ones. In this work, the validation was conducted in the Cadence Virtuoso tool where the symbol, testbench circuits, and simulation conditions were defined. Furthermore, a comparative analysis is presented between the experimentally obtained data and the corresponding modeled outcomes, demonstrating favorable outcomes that validate the rigor of this study.

articleTitle: Tomato Disease Detection Using Quaternion Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Plant disease is a crucial problem for the agricultural industry, and timely detection of plant diseases is a most concerning task. Today, more and more technologies are born with the aim of timely detecting plant diseases, especially for tomatoes, to improve crop quality. Therefore, our research proposed a solution for classifying tomato leaf diseases using the Quaternion Convolutional Neural Network based on VGG16 architecture. In this model, the pixel value is represented by a supercomplex number instead of real numbers, as in CNN models. This method preserves the structural information of color values in a single pixel or image region. The dataset used in this paper is taken from PlantVillage with ten different types of diseases. The results show that the accuracy of the proposed algorithm outperforms the other methods and achieves up to 93% with 100 epochs.

articleTitle: Design and Calibration of Multi-Channel Thermocouple Signal Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Thermocouples are widely used as sensors for measuring temperature due to their high sensitivity and wide range, but they require an interface with Analog-to-Digital Converters. (ADCs). This article presents a design approach for a multi-channel thermocouple converter, enhancing accuracy, performance, and flexibility, while also examining the impact of heat rise rate on temperature values.

articleTitle: Tightly-coupled GPS/INS/Lidar Integration for Road Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Navigation systems integrating multiple sensors with high data rates, high accuracy, and all-weather conditions are widely used for autonomous robots. This paper proposes a tightly coupled GPS/INS/LIDAR integration system to achieve highly accurate position, real-time state estimation and mapping. This system formulates lidar-inertial integration and GPS information, including loop closures. We will build an EKF algorithm for three-axis orientation estimation to improve the robot’s position and orientation in the GPS/INS/LIDAR integration system. The estimated motion from three-axis orientation estimation will be used to produce an initial prediction for lidar odometry information. The bias of the gyros and accelerometers in IMU is estimated using the lidar odometry solution. We discard old lidar scans for pose optimization, and then introduce new keyframes to ensure high performance in real-time. Experiment results show that our proposed integration system gives the RMS positioning error of less than 1 meter. The RMS orientation error of Euler angles is less than 2 degrees.

articleTitle: An efficient method to calculate power transformers’ frequency response from a state-space model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Frequency response analysis of power transformers and reactors can reveal mechanical and electrical defects in windings’ structure. Interpretation of a response though, is not an easy task for inexperienced engineers. Furthermore, an in-depth study of windings’ failure requires either practical, physical or mathematical models. Building complex circuits to model the power transformers’ frequency response is tedious; that is where state-space modeling comes in handy. The main problem is that the state-space model requires symbolic calculations, which are not always feasible on low-end computers. This paper shall introduce a symbolic-free method to calculate the transfer function of power transformers and reactors from their state-space model.

articleTitle: An Improved Neural Network Algorithm for Optimal Installation and Operation of Battery Energy Storage System in Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Integrating distributed generations (DGs) into the power system has significantly increased the significance of battery energy storage systems (BESS) in improving system performance. This research aims to define the optimal BESS installation and operation using an Improved Neural Network Algorithm (INNA) to maximize its benefits within the radial distribution system (RDS) integrated with DGs. The INNA integrates a Simple Quadratic Interpolation (SQI) strategy to improve searchability. The optimal BESS installation and operation problem aims to reduce the energy cost of RDS purchased from the main substation. This study investigates four cases of IEEE 33-bus RDS over 24 hours of a representative day with time-of-use electricity tariffs. The simulation results show that the INNA application for optimal BESS installation and operation is very promising in reducing energy cost and energy loss of RDS integrated with DGs.

articleTitle: Antenna Selection in Energy Harvesting NOMA Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Energy harvesting (EH) non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) networks exploit the advantages of both EH and NOMA for high energy efficiency and spectral efficiency. To further improve these efficiencies as well as communication reliability, the deployment of multiple antennas at the NOMA transmitter is necessary so as for it to collect more energy from the power transmitter and perform the antenna selection. This paper analyzes the throughput of the proposed antenna selection scheme in EH NOMA networks under realistic EH paradigm and general wireless channels. Various results demonstrate that the characteristic of EH drastically deteriorates communication reliability. Additionally, EH NOMA networks may suffer the worst performance for improper specification selection. In addition, increasing the quantity of antennas ameliorates network performance significantly. Furthermore, the antenna selection influences dramatically the performance gap between NOMA terminals.

articleTitle: Derivation of Small-Signal Model of Boost-SEPIC Interleaved Converter Based on PWM Switch Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Small-signal model is essential in ensuring the quality and performance of dc-dc converters. An insight into dynamics is a fundamental requirement to select and design the controller of converters correctly. The dc-dc boost-SEPIC interleaved (BSI) converter has the potential for wide application but the small-signal model has not been thoroughly studied. This paper presents a method to establish the small-signal model of the high-order BSI converter based on the circuit averaging and averaged switch techniques. The transfer function model obtained in factorized form with three complex poles, two complex zeros, and one real zero makes it convenient to analyze characteristics and evaluate the impact of components and working conditions on the dynamic of the converter. The obtained model is verified by simulation and experimental results on the frequency domain.

articleTitle: Studying Short Discharge Method for Re-used Lead-acid Car Battery SOH Evaluation under Variable Discharge Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Rural electrification has the potential to significantly contribute to economic and social growth in many developing nations. However, expensive energy systems are out of reach for many people and renewable energies available in these countries are critical to reducing the environmental impact of such systems. To address this issue, frugal innovation based on re-purposed materials can provide cost-effective and long-term solutions. The possibility of reusing discarded lead acid batteries from thermal engine cars in renewable energy systems is investigated in this paper. Before these batteries can be used, their State of Health (SoH) must be accurately and efficiently assessed, but the devices and the method should remain simple and cheap.In this perspective, this paper investigates the possibility of using a basic lab resistor to achieve the two pulse method for SoH assessment of several batteries. The accuracy is evaluated by a comparison with a measurement derived from an electronic load. In the final system, this will be accomplished by reusing power electronics devices coming from discarded desktop Power Supply Units (PSUs). By recycling waste materials and using economical testing techniques, this strategy can give people access to renewable energy options that are both affordable and sustainable.

articleTitle: Flexible Consensus Mechanism for Current Allocation in DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Renewable energy sources (RESs) have become the predominant trend in the development of energy systems in many countries. To coordinate RESs, microgrids have emerged as an efficient and optimal solution. However, the microgrid is facing the problem of inaccurate power sharing between the generators. To address the issue, this paper proposes a control technique that combines a dynamic consensus with droop control algorithms. The proposed method calculates current sharing error by utilizing current values and consensus algorithm. Then, an external current-sharing controller is adopted to regulate the droop parameter in an inner controller for improving the current sharing among RESs. By applying the proposed control method, the current sharing accuracy is achieved in the microgrid system under different load conditions. The proposed technique is analyzed and evaluated with the scale-down microgrid consisting of three distributed generators. The simulation results of the scale-down microgrid are obtained from the PLECS simulation platform.

articleTitle: A combined neural network model for forecasting solar energy from multiple weather parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The article aims to propose a combined neural network model to forecast the solar energy of a solar power plant. Predicting solar energy is extremely important in planning, investing in electricity development, and operating the power system. Solar power integration in electrical grids is complicated due to its dependence on volatile weather conditions. Artificial neural networks have been employed in recent years to solve the problem. Two well-known models, the Nonlinear autoregressive exogenous model (NARX) and the Long-short term memory (LSTM), are suitable methods for determining photovoltaic (PV) output forecasting. This article proposes a two-stage model combining the NARX and LSTM to forecast the output energy of a solar power plant. The proposed model has been evaluated and compared with NARX and LSTM. The data have been collected at Son My 3.1 Solar Power Plant project from the monitoring system with electrical power, solar irradiance, wind speed, and wind direction, from July 1, 2019, to June 30, 2020. A general score based on three error functions, Mean squared error, Mean absolute error, and R-squared, is the indicator to investigate the forecasting efficiency of the methods. The numerical results show that the combined NARX-LSTM model is better than other methods in this study.

articleTitle: A 6-18-GHz GaN High Power Amplifier with Excellent Gain Flatness
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper presents a monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) reactive matching power amplifier (RMPA) designed using a 150 nm AlGaN/GaN on SiC technology, showcasing its exceptional gain flatness of only 3dB across the 6-18 GHz band. The three-stage RMPA operates in pulsed mode with a pulse-width of 100-µsec and a duty cycle of 10%, delivering impressive performance metrics. It achieves a maximum output power of 43.5 dBm (equivalent to 22.4 watts) and a maximum efficiency of 25%, while maintaining a linear gain of 22 dB under a bias condition of 28 V drain voltage and 620 mA quiescent drain current. The MMIC PA has a small dimension of 4.5 mm × 4.05 mm.

articleTitle: Applying Artificial Intelligence To Distribution Network State Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The paper focuses on researching and building a program to estimate the state of the distribution network with two different methods: the weighted least squares (WLS) and the artificial neural network (ANN) using the Python programming language. Firstly, both methods are used to compute the standard IEEE 118-bus system. The state estimation results of voltage and phase angle are compared with those calculated by Newton-Raphson method in steady-state power flow problem. Furthermore, the paper presents the computed results applied to the real distribution network to demonstrate the effectiveness of state estimation problem for power systems. Datasets are generated by altering loads n times at buses in distribution networks. Each time loads are modified, power flow calculations are performed to record powers, voltages, and phase angles. Finally, the advantages and disadvantages of each method are evaluated to facilitate practical applications.

articleTitle: Back-stepping Technique-based Distributed Formation Control of Multiple Under-actuated Autonomous Underwater Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper focuses on a distributed formation control for multiple under-actuated autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) with prescribed performance subject to external disturbance. First, distributed formation tracking errors are calculated using graph theory and state transformation. The errors are dexterously transformed into new error variables to satisfy the predefined performance. Based on the back-stepping procedure, the distributed formation controller is then developed and combined with a nonlinear disturbance observer (NDO) to enhance the robustness against external disturbances. It is mathematically proven that the proposed formation controller guarantees that all signals in the whole control system are uniformly ultimately bounded (UUB) and the distributed formation tracking errors always remain within the predefined regions. Finally, numerical simulations verify the proposed controller's effectiveness and feasibility.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a 6-18 GHz Multi-Stage Wideband GaN LNA with 16.5 dBm OP1dB and over 42 dBm Survivability
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: A 6-18 GHz multi-stage wideband Gallium Nitride (GaN) Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) with high linearity and high robustness is presented. A feedback amplifier circuit with gain enhancement and reactive impedance matching networks can compensate for transistors gain roll-off with frequency to achieve a better gain-flatness and extend overall bandwidth. The feedback values are chosen different for each stage by optimizing the frequency response of each unit cell to obtain low noise, good return loss, high gain and high linearity simultaneously. The 1-dB compression point output power (OP1dB) contours and Gp circles are drawn on the same load impedance complex plane to identify optimum impedance for the last stage. The LNA in 0.25 µm GaN pHEMT process achieves 2-2.7 dB noise figure (NF), 25.4 dB average gain with ±1.3 dB gain-flatness, 10.5 dB input return loss and 12 dB output return loss. The LNA exhibits OP1dB of 16.5 dBm, output third-order intercept point (OIP3) of 30 dBm and robustness up to 42 dBm input power level, showing the strong potential for radar and electronic warfare (EW) applications.

articleTitle: Study on Subsynchronous Resonance in Vietnam Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The SSR is a concerning issue in power systems that can lead to damaging consequences such as turbine-generator shaft damage and power system instability. The installation of series capacitors on transmission lines is a major factor contributing to SSR. Vietnam experienced an occurrence of SSR at the Vung Ang I thermal power plant on November 24th, 2015. As the country’s renewable energy sector, particularly wind turbine generators, continues to expand rapidly, the severity of SSR to Vietnam power system is expected to increase. Recognizing the significant harms caused by SSR to power systems, this article focuses on studying this phenomenon in the power grid of Vietnam under two typical scenarios: 2020 and 2025. The research makes use the EMTP-RV tool to determine the frequency range that triggers SSR and identifies power plants at high risk of being affected. In addition, a viable solution for reducing SSR in the power system is proposed and validated.

articleTitle: A study on dummy signal processing of targets for the self-propelled artillery
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The self-propelled artillery is one of the weapons with high mobility and very effective in supporting infantry to master battlefields. It is equipped with a radar to capture targets and control weapons to destroy targets. Normaly, the cabin of the vehicle is too small, therefore the commander cannot monitor the crew's actions to improve the effectiveness of the practical training. In this paper, the authors have conducted a research on pseudo-signal generation for self-propelled artillery radars then transmitting them to computers as a basis step for the improving research and training systems. To carry out the above research, the authors conducted a practical survey of signal parameters on the real equipment then combined them with the technical documents to analyze and select signals to be transmitted to the experiment computer. Study about methods for simulating the pseudo-signal generation of targets, signal transceiver and display technology on self-propelled artillery radar screen through programming of the STM32-F411 microcontroller and the application of Lora technology (Long Range Radio) to transmit and receive signals. The research results through hard and software experiments have shown as a basis step for evaluating the effectiveness of the design.

articleTitle: The Efficiency of High-performance SHA-3 Accelerator on the System Level
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The Secure Hash Algorithm-3 (SHA-3) has become increasingly vital in numerous security applications within the Internet of Things (IoT) field. Given the diverse purposes, SHA-3 serves in the IoT landscape, the need for versatility is essential. Additionally, recent studies have primarily focused on achieving high performance and optimizing resource utilization for SHA-3. However, these studies have overlooked the crucial aspect of data transfer between the external memory and the hash function block, as transfer time plays a significant role. This paper proposes an efficient SHA-3 architecture designed for System-on-Chip (SoC) based on a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) called system-level SHA-3 accelerator (SSA) to address the aforementioned challenges and be suitable for real edge computing. The SSA contains three key proposals. Firstly, the proposed padding architecture is designed from a combination of Serial Input to Parallel Output (SIPO) and a barrel shifter, which is well-suitable for managing the data transfer process on the system. Secondly, implementing a two-stage pipelining within the Round Function (RF) to reduce critical path delays and make a high occupancy. Finally, designing four modes (SHA3-224, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, and SHA3-512) enables the SSA to compute various SHA-3 to support a wide range of applications. Our architecture is implemented on the DE10-Standard Development Kit (Cyclone V SX SoC-5CSXFC6D6F31C6N), which is integrated into the FPGA and is controlled by a Dual-Core ARM Cortex-A9 processor. The result is up to 38.34 Gbps in throughput and 5.61 Mbps/ALM in efficiency for the RF computation, 28.02 Gbps in throughput, and 3.63 Mbps/ALM for the full proposed architecture.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Anti-Attack methods for RPL routing protocol in 6LoWPAN networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Scientific and technological advancements, particularly in IoT, have greatly enhanced the quality of life in society. Nevertheless, resource constrained IoT devices are now connected to the Internet through IPv6 and 6LoWPAN networks, which are often unreliable and untrusted. Securing these devices with robust security measures poses a significant challenge. Despite implementing encryption and authentication, these devices remain vulnerable to wireless attacks from within the 6LoWPAN network and from the Internet. Researchers have developed various methods to prevent attacks on the RPL protocol within the 6LoWPAN network. However, each method can only detect a limited number of attack types, and there are still several drawbacks that require improvement. This study aims to implement several attack prevention methods, such as Lightweight Heartbeat Protocol, SVELTE, and Contiki IDS. The study will provide an overview of these methods' theories and simulate them on Contiki OS using Cooja software to assess their performance. The study's results demonstrate a correlation between the simulated data and the proposed theories. Furthermore, the study identifies and evaluates the strengths and weaknesses of these methods, highlighting areas that can be improved upon.

articleTitle: A Design of Source-Switched Charge Pump Circuit with 65nm Technology by using Bayesian Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: A charge pump (CP) has been one of the most widely used components in many phase-lock loops (PLLs), and new topologies of the CP have been created a lot these days to optimize certain variables. This paper presents a method for designing CP circuits and applying the AI algorithm to optimize power consumption of the CP. The study proposes using the Bayesian optimization (BO) algorithm to design and optimize the source-switched CP circuit. In this work, the width and length variables of each transistor in the CP circuit were found by the BO algorithm to reduce the power consumption of the circuit. After being optimized, the power consumption parameter was lowered by 73.6%, from 2.58mW to 0.67mW. Although the power consumption of the circuit fell significantly, it was not the global minimum of the power consumption of the source-switched CP circuit. Thus, further research would be required to find the global minimal power consumption of the source-switched CP circuit and improve other parameters of the CP circuit, such as jitter and performance.

articleTitle: A Memory-Saving Approach for 5G New Radio Low-Density Parity-Check Decoders
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: This paper presents a memory efficient design for a Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) decoder. The design is based on a combination of two techniques that consists of (i) the proposed Enhanced single minimum Min-Sum (EsmMS) algorithm for check-node update processing, which requires only the first minimum value among variable-to-check input messages and its index instead of two minima, and (ii) the memory split method, which adapts to the varying check-node degree of 5G LDPC codes. The implementation results on Xilinx Kintex UltraScale+ (xcku5p) FPGA show that the proposed decoder requires 37% less storage space than MS-based decoders, provides a decoding throughput of 2.63 Gbps, while yielding a decoding gain up to 0.32 dB at the BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> compared to the Min-Sum decoder.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Perceptron Learning Algorithm for Day-Ahead Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: The output power of a photovoltaic system depends on weather conditions. It’s well established that the power output efficiencies from solar photovoltaic (PV) systems is very much dependent on weather parameters and deposited solid particles on the panel surface. This paper aims to address the demand for a more accurate prediction of their operational performance in order to maximise their contribution to the overall energy mix. This research applies Perceptron Learning Algorithm to forecast the day-head PV generation capacity whilst considering future and historical meteorological parameters and system data. Model evaluation results, for an ensuing 24-hour ahead period of interest, achieved forecast accuracy in excess of 90% compared to the recorded power from an installed campus-based micro-grid array.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Dynamic Multiprotocol with Forwarding Service on a Radio Co-Processor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Internet of Things protocols such as ZigBee, Thread and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) are the popular low-power protocols developed for interconnection among wireless devices in IoT systems using the same frequency spectrum. In this paper we propose a general mechanism providing the concurrent multiple protocol operation on a radio co-processor with can support seamless connections to multiple standard IoT devices. Dynamic multiprotocol technique allows a network node to run BLE and IEEE 805.14 standard stacks simultaneously. Additionally, by implementing a service called forwarding service on top of the BLE and Thread stacks, a connection between a Thread-only node and a BLE application can be established through a BLE/Thread multiprotocol node acting as a forwarder. Moreover, remote control and observation of the multiprotocol network from the Internet are enabled by using the popular MQTT protocol. To demonstrate the benefits of our proposed mechanism for various IoT applications, a deep performance evaluation is conducted in a real testbed with several scenarios.

articleTitle: Integration of AI and SNOMED CT in Chest X-Ray Diagnosis Software System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: In the medical field, the application of artificial intelligence (AI), especially deep learning models of convolutional neural networks (CNN) to disease diagnosis is becoming more and more popular. However, the research and application of AI in disease diagnosis in Vietnam is still limited. Disease prediction is still fragmentary, there is no link between clinical and laboratory results, as well as the problem of disease identification is not synchronized and consistent among studies because labels are described in text that can be confusing, especially in the medical field. Therefore, this research paper applies Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine-Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) as a set of electronic clinical terminology in labeling input data for machine learning in the field of medical pathology diagnosis as well as making suggestion of the templates for each specific disease. Specifically, the article evaluates the results of a method of diagnosing abnormalities in chest X-ray (XR) images based on the Densenet-121 network architecture and normalizing the forms based on SNOMED CT codes. DICOM medical images are obtained directly and automatically from the X-ray modality through the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) at Telemedicine and Mobile Healthcare lab, Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology. Chest abnormalities are detected, classified and returned to the SNOMECD CT codes corresponding to the major problems in the sample template on workstation using the AI TOOL ASSISTANT software system. A survey of 222 actual abnormally diagnosed chest X-rays images at the international clinic participating in the trial showed that the accurate of the prediction results was 82% when compared with the doctor's conclusions according to these samples.

articleTitle: DETopK: training for DETR based models with Top K predictions noise
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: DETR is one of the first object detection models to apply the attention mechanism, which was proven to be very strong for many machine learning models. There have been many variants of DETR that can achieve competitive results on the COCO dataset, proving the DETR line’s capabilities of creating state-of-the-art models. In this paper, we present DETopK - a simple training method for DETR based models that focus on the detection area of object queries. Because of hardware limitation (2080Ti GPU), our experiment was performed with Deformable DETR multi-scale, on COCO-minitrain - a subset of the COCO dataset for a reasonable training time. It is very encouraging that the experimental results show that the proposed method helps Deformable DETR gain 0.27% in AP, 0.36% in AR and better accuracy overall when trained with our method.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered ℋ∞ Optimal Control for Euler-Lagrange Dynamics with Dead Zone Inputs under Attacks on Sensors and Actuators
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Optimal control has been investigated for Euler-Lagrange (EL) systems. However, the existing methods have not yet considered the input constraints due to dead zones and vulnerabilities caused by malicious attackers. In this paper, we propose a novel control algorithm to gain the bounded ℒ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-gain tracking performance with deadzone disturbance rejection and to reduce not only the effects of sensor and actuator attacks but also the burden of communication load. Firstly, an event-triggered (ET) observer is studied to conjecture the unmeasurable states and compensate for the adverse attack effects. Secondly, ET augmented control is proposed to transform Euler-Lagrange dynamics into tracking error dynamics. Thirdly, an ET ${{\mathcal{H}}_\infty }$ optimal control law is approximated via adaptive dynamic programming (ADP). Finally, the simulation of mobile nonholonomic robots illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Application of Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Faults of Grid-tied Solar Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Solar energy has always been an extensively researched field worldwide. One of the key concerns is diagnosing and addressing faults in grid-tied solar power systems. Solar panels, as vital components of these systems, are prone to various issues including short circuit, open circuit, discoloration and surface cracks. Similarly, DC/DC or DC/AC converters often encounter semiconductor component failures due to prolonged high-frequency switching. This paper aims to comprehensively investigate and propose diagnostic methods for grid-tied solar power systems. The suggested faults for diagnosis encompass shading, shorts, and mixed faults in PV array, as well as shorts and open circuits in diodes and switches of the DC/DC boost converter. Additionally, shorts in sub-modules of the modular multilevel converter (MMC) are considered. To identify these faults, analysis of I-V curve of PV strings, diode voltage signals from the boost converter and three-phase output voltage of MMC is conducted. Finally, the faults are extracted by feature extraction algorithms, preprocessed by Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and classified by Support Vector Machines (SVM) – an artificial intelligence technique. Overall, this research provides novel insights and develops high-accuracy predictive models, achieving accuracy levels of nearly 90%.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Optimization for IRS-Aided Multiuser MIMO SWIPT Cognitive Radio Systems with Imperfect CSI
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ISEE)
abstract: Cognitive radio (CR) techniques have been widely recognized as an effective solution to utilize the radio spectrum resource. An integration of intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) into the CR systems is expected to yield further enhancements in spectral efficiency (SE) and energy efficiency (EE). This paper explores the achievable EE performance of multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) systems under the scenario of nonlinear energy harvesting model and imperfection of channel state information (CSI). The optimal design of transmit precoding (TPC) matrices at the secondary base station (SBS), the phase shift matrix at the IRS, and energy harvesting (EH) power splitting (PS) factors at the users to maximize the EE is challenging due to the fractional nature of the objective function, nonconvex constraints of coupled design variables and robust semi-infinite interference power (IP) constraints. To deal with non-convexity, we seek appropriate surrogate functions and convex inner sets. To handle the semi-infinite IP constraints, we recast them as linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Then, we introduce an iterative algorithm utilizing alternating optimization (AO) and the Dinkelbach method to find optimal solutions. Through extensive simulations, we gain the insights into the effectiveness of the EE optimization scheme against the SE optimization approach.
